title: Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods
summary: Toei's 2013 theatrical feature (85 min; 105 min special edition) — the first Dragon Ball film whose story Toriyama wrote himself, and, measured against this owner's instrument (his Dragon Ball manga, AniList 30042, ch 1-519), an ORIGINAL: it adapts no chapter, because every source that places it puts the story in the gap BETWEEN two of them. PLACEMENT, FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCES, ONE SLOT: (1) Toei's press release of 2012-07-17 — 「アニメーションシリーズの「Ｚ」と「ＧＴ」の間、つまり、原作517話で魔人ブウとの戦いが終わった後、518話までの空白の10年の間に起こったエピソードが初めて描かれる」 (same page: 原作 鳥山明 / 監督 細田雅弘 / 脚本 渡辺雄介); (2) ANN 2012-07-14 reporting Weekly Shōnen Jump #33 — 'set between the 517th and 518th installments of Akira Toriyama's original manga… during the "lost decade"'; (3) ja-WP 神と神 概要 — 「原作の第517話と第518話、『ドラゴンボールZ』の第288話と第289話、『ドラゴンボール改』の第157話と第158話の間」, cited to 「DRAGON BALL年代記」『鳥山明 The world of DRAGON BALL パンフレット』東映 2013-03-27 (Age 778, about four years after Buu); (4) dragonball.fandom Timeline placement — 'As a continuation of the manga, its events take place between the manga chapters 517 and 518'. Zero source pages in it → filler (T27), no chapters (A1). TORIYAMA'S CREDIT IS A CREDIT (T26): Toei credits him 原作, the theatre pamphlet 「原作・ストーリー・キャラクターデザイン 鳥山明」, and ja-WP (citing 日経エンタテインメント! 2013年5月号) records the mechanism — 「鳥山がコミックの原作と違わぬほど書き込んだ台詞入りプロットの中から90%以上のストーリーと台詞が採用されている」; the screenplay credit is 渡辺雄介's. His manga finished in 1995 and never took the film's events in, so there is no adoption to record on this shelf — and none anywhere: see the note on `adopted`. THE TRAP THIS ROW SETS FOR A CURATOR: the licensor calls the film canon. Toei's release ends 「スピンオフでも番外編でもない、ドラゴンボール正史のストーリーが誕生する」 and 『ドラゴンボール超全集3』 (Shueisha 2013-02-10, p.30) says 「言わば正史である」. That is franchise CONTINUITY, not chapter coverage; T25/T27 measure the row against the source's pages, and there are none. (The only manga pages in the film are decorative — dragonball.fandom's trivia notes the end credits display kanzenban pages.) THE DELIVERABLE ON THIS SHELF IS THE POSITION: the stored 291.5 is the halo's air-date derivation (a 2013 film after a 1996 finale) and it is three rows late — ja-WP names the slot in this owner's own numbering, between eps 288 and 289, and our own anchors agree with that seam.

position.why: CORRECTED 291.5 → 288.5. ja-WP states the slot in this owner's own episode numbering — 『ドラゴンボールZ』の第288話と第289話の間 — and it is the same seam Toei, WSJ #33 (via ANN) and dragonball.fandom give in chapter space (between ch 517 and 518). ROW IDENTITY CHECKED BY TITLE AND DATE, NEVER BY INDEX (R20): en-WP's Dragon Ball Z season 9 table gives 287 'Celebrations with Majin Buu' = 戻った平和!!正義の味方魔人ブウ!? (1995-12-20), 288 'He's Always Late' = 遅いぜ悟空！みんなでパーティ!! (1996-01-10), 289 'Granddaughter Pan' = 悟空おじいちゃん！私がパンよ!! (1996-01-17) — title for title and date for date with the stored grid, so ja-WP's 第288話/第289話 are our rows 288/289. OUR ANCHORS AGREE WITH THE SEAM: ep 287 → ch 517, ep 288 filler (the barbecue), ep 289 → ch 517-518 (the ten-years-later 28th Tenka'ichi Budokai). The film is Age 778 — four years after Kid Buu, six years before that tournament (dragonball.fandom's Timeline placement) — so it belongs after the last row before the jump. Toriyama's own reason for choosing the gap is on the record (ja-WP, from his オフィシャルムービーガイド and Vジャンプ interviews): 「悟空たちが一番強い時期であること」, and after the final chapter Goku has gone off with Uub while Bulma and Krillin have visibly aged. The stored 291.5 is only the air-date derivation (the row's own note says 'position derived from the air date (a proposal)') and it would show a viewer Uub, the tournament and Goku's departure before a film set six years earlier. ALTERNATIVE IF SEAN PREFERS IT: 291.5 has a release-order defence (the film is sold as the sequel to the Z series and every home-video line lists it after the run). My recommendation is the licensor's slot, 288.5, with the release-order fact in the note. Whichever way it goes, dragon-ball-z-kai's row is the same decision — that verdict proposes 165.5, the identical point in Kai's international numbering.

flags_for_sean: POSITION IS THE DECISION HERE: 291.5 (stored, air-date derivation) → 288.5 (the licensor's placement; ja-WP's explicit episode slot; corroborated by our own anchors 287 → 517, 288 filler, 289 → 517-518). The alternative — keep 291.5 on the release-order convention — is stated in position.why. The dragon-ball-z-kai row is the same call (98.5 → 165.5); rule the two together.

正史 IS NOT A STANDING. Toei ('スピンオフでも番外編でもない、ドラゴンボール正史のストーリー') and 超全集3 ('言わば正史である') both call the film official history; under T25/T27 the row is still filler because no page of ch 1-519 is animated in it. One clause in the ledger note would keep a reader from being surprised: 'official continuity, but no chapter of the manga is in it — it happens inside the ten-year gap at ch 517/518.'

NO ADOPTION ON ANY SHELF, AND THAT IS A RULED FACT, NOT MY INFERENCE. THE ADOPTION QUESTION IS ALREADY RULED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Sean, 2026-09-05 (the T26 adoption sitting + batch 22 wave 2, lib/rulings/episode-types.ts T30 pin on DBS ep 6 and lib/rulings/applied/batch-22.ts): 'NO adopted{author} (the bar is 脚本; this film's 脚本 is 渡辺雄介)' — Resurrection 'F' cleared that bar (原作・脚本 鳥山明), Battle of Gods does not. My research CONFIRMS the distinction rather than reopening it: ja-WP draws exactly the same line — 「正確には『神と神』では9割以上の原案・プロットを担当、『復活のF』では初めて脚本を担当した」. So no `adopted` record belongs on any of this film's three rows. The film's material did enter the DRAGON BALL SUPER manga (ch 1-4, 2015) — but on that parallel owner the catalog already records the relationship as a SHARED ARC with correspondence rows (lib/rulings/arcs.ts, A46: 'Battle of Gods', kind shared, eps 1-14 ↔ ch 1-4), which is the instrument for it. Nothing of it touches this owner's instrument, which closed in 1995.

SHELF CONSISTENCY: this agrees with the applied dragon-ball-z triage (out/triage__dragon-ball-z.json — 18/18 originals, 'NO ADOPTION ANYWHERE ON THIS SHELF'). Battle of Gods is the nineteenth original on that shelf; it differs only in that the author wrote it and a LATER, DIFFERENT manga tells the same story.

MECHANICS: the move frees 291.5 and lands on 288.5. planRuledMoves refuses a ruled slot held by a non-moving row — nothing in the context suggests 288.5 is occupied (the post-1996 DBZ extras cluster at 291.5x, which this move empties rather than fills), but the dry run should confirm.

THE HALO NOTE POINTS THE WRONG WAY: the stored row says 'adapts the series' own instrument: Dragon Ball Super (MANGA)'. The AniList edge behind that is the MANGA node's ADAPTATION edge (86508 → 14837 — the manga adapts the film; batch-20 verifier, research/batch20/verify/dragon-ball-super-w5a.md): the protocol's comicalization trap read from the wrong end. On THIS owner the film adapts nothing at all, and the ruled note should say so.
